audit.whatIsWrong: The stored chart (Skill, Yasuo, Yasuo, Skill, Skill, Yasuo, Yasuo) contradicts its own whys[] text and the mirror.
audit.why: whys[0], whys[1] and whys[2] all explicitly say Gnar wins levels 1, 2 and 3, while win[]/phases[].side said Skill, Yasuo, Yasuo — the page renders two different answers. The mirror audit set the chart to Gnar, Gnar, Gnar, Gnar, Skill, Gnar, Yasuo as one atomic group, so I match it and rewrite whys[3], whys[4] and whys[5] to agree.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1, 2, 3 and 5 flipped in both layers with ratings rescaled; whys[3..5] rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere despite the whole matchup being cooldown-timed.
audit.why: Boomerang Throw 16/14.5/13/11.5/10, Hop 22/19.5/17/14.5/12, Wallop/Hyper 7s flat, GNAR! 90/60/30, Last Breath 70/50/30, Wind Wall 25s at rank 1 for a 4s wall.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into spikes[0], spikes[1], spikes[2], phases[4].why and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mega Gnar's stun is called 'GNAR! (W stun)'; Mega's engage is called a Boomerang; and 'Last Breath converts ANY knockup'.
audit.why: GNAR! is the R. The Mega W is Wallop, a melee smash — it passes straight through Wind Wall, which only stops projectiles (Boomerang Throw / Boulder Toss). Mega's gap-close is Crunch (E), not a boomerang. And Last Breath needs an airborne target: Gnar's knockups land on you, so your only setup is your own two-stack Steel Tempest whirlwind.
audit.corrected: Wallop named as the melee stun that ignores Wind Wall; Boulder Toss named as the wall target; Q2 whirlwind named as the only Last Breath setup.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 read Skill because your Q3 knock-up and Sweeping Blade mobility finally match his hop-kite.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay Gnar — his poke range still beats your 475 Q even as your Sweeping Blade mobility grows.

edits.before: Level 6 flips to Yasuo since Last Breath punishes any transform or Boomerang whiff once you can dash in.
edits.after: Level 6 is a skill check — Last Breath punishes a whiffed Boomerang, but Mega Gnar's stun answers your dash.

edits.before: At first item your crit-backed Q3-into-R burst out-damages mini Gnar in every all-in.
edits.after: At first item Gnar edges it: Mega form's bulk and CC still beat your burst window.

edits.before: Mini Gnar kites you with Boomerang Throw (Q) and Hop (E), poking free while you eat minion aggro chasing the catch — respect his Rage bar and back off as it fills.
edits.after: Mini Gnar kites with Boomerang Throw (Q, 16s at rank 1) and Hop (E, 22s) — chasing the catch pulls minion aggro. Back off as his Rage bar fills toward the transform.

edits.before: Once you hit 6 and can flow-shield E-Q through his poke, the threat inverts: a mistimed Gnar transform with no wall behind him lets you Sweeping Blade in and R his airborne combo.
edits.after: At 6 the threat inverts only while he is in mini form: Sweeping Blade in, Q2 whirlwind for the knockup, then Last Breath. GNAR! is 90s at rank 1 — count it before you commit.

edits.before: With early crit online your Q3 knock-up plus R turns any GNAR! (W stun) or Boomerang whiff into a full burst rotation before he can Hop away.
edits.after: With early crit your Q2 whirlwind into Last Breath punishes a whiffed Boulder Toss — but Wallop (W) is Mega's stun, not GNAR!, and it is only 7s.

edits.before: You out-DPS mini Gnar in extended trades; only mega Gnar's Wallop and GNAR! CC threaten you, and Wind Wall eats his Boomerang engage.
edits.after: You out-DPS mini Gnar in extended trades; Mega's Wallop smash is melee and passes through Wind Wall, so save the wall for Boulder Toss.

edits.before: With items and crit you win extended fights against mini Gnar outright and can Wind Wall mega Gnar's Boomerang engage; only a clean GNAR! stun into Wallop flips a fight, so bait his transform and burst him down.
edits.after: With items and crit you win extended fights against mini Gnar outright, and Wind Wall eats Boulder Toss; only a clean Wallop stun flips a fight, so bait his transform and burst him while Rage drains.

edits.before: Wind Wall his Boomerang Throw return path or mega-Gnar Boomerang
edits.after: Wind Wall his Boomerang Throw and Mega Gnar's Boulder Toss

edits.before: Last Breath converts ANY knockup into a kill window. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Gnar's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Last Breath (70s at rank 1) needs your own Q2 whirlwind — Gnar's own knockups do not feed it. GNAR! is 90s at rank 1.

edits.before: Last Breath converts ANY knockup into a kill window — build your teamfight around that. Gnar carry threat: 8/10 — shift to picks and wave control if he gets ahead.
edits.after: Last Breath needs an airborne target and only your own Q2 whirlwind gives one. Gnar carry threat: 8/10 — shift to picks and wave control if he gets ahead.

edits.before: - Gnar GNAR!: matchup-defining — His Mega all-in. Fight mini form. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Gnar GNAR! (R): 90s at rank 1 — his Mega all-in, so fight him in mini form. - Wallop is only 7s and passes through Wind Wall. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.

notes: The packet chart (Gnar, Gnar, Gnar, Skill, Yasuo, Yasuo, Yasuo) and the mirror chart (Gnar, Gnar, Gnar, Gnar, Skill, Gnar, Yasuo) disagree. Per the mirror rule I followed the mirror so the two directions cannot contradict, and rewrote whys[3..5] to match. If the user prefers the packet, this is the one matchup in my slice to revisit. The kit's projectile flag on GNAR! (R) contradicts a displacement effect, so I made no claim about Wind Wall stopping it.
